# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined

`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,

      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }

Now I understand the two incident fixes:

**Fix 1 — cross-version key-slot stability:**
- `CustomProviderRegistry.keySlotCandidates(baseUrl, providerName)` — canonical-first family of slot names.
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots(migrations, keys)` in headless_provider_key.dart — boot-time non-destructive copy from a stranded legacy slot to the canonical one, with stderr notices; keychain in scope; failure degrades to notice.
- `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — carries the whole family in the secrets snapshot.
- Called from `bin/fah_runapp.dart` BEFORE any resolution, on stderr.
- Presumably `ModelRolesResolver._endpointScopedKeyNames` (resolver fallbacks) now probes the family too — let me check the rest of the model_resolver diff.

**Fix 2 — missing-key degrade:**
- New `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException`; `UnknownProviderRoleException` now extends it; the no-usable-entry throw ALWAYS throws the degradable type (missing-key chains no longer hard-exit the boot).
- Boot boundary (fah_runapp) catches `UnusableRoleChainException` → warn + fall back to legacy single-model path.

Security/behavior review of these changes:
1. `migrateLegacyKeySlots` copies a key VALUE from one slot to another within the SAME endpoint — key material never crosses endpoints (S4/I4 preserved). The migration sources are the user's own saved entries + roles refs. Non-destructive. Notice names slots, not values. ✓ S3-safe.
2. `keys.save(canonical, value)` — writes through to OS keychain. Failure → notice with `keys.lastSaveError` — need to check lastSaveError exists and doesn't leak the value. Let me check SecureKeyCache.save/available/lastSaveError.
3. Missing-key degrade: a boot with all roles missing keys now falls back to the legacy single-model path with a warning — is that SAFE? The concern: previously a loud failure; now silently-ish boots on the configured single provider/model. The warning is on stderr. The user still gets a working session (can /key set). This matches the incident requirement. But there's a subtle risk: the fallback model might be a DIFFERENT provider than the user intended (the "measures the wrong provider" class). The warning names it though ("falling back to the configured single provider/model"). This was an owner-demanded fix per the incident threads. OK.

Let me now check:
- The rest of model_resolver.dart diff (endpoint-scoped key names probing the family).
- SecureKeyCache.lastSaveError/available existence.
- The new/changed tests: custom_providers_test (REG), poisoned_provider_boot_test (+43 boot-level IT), model_resolver_test (+58), startup_test.
- CI status on head 0a4201475.
- Run the verification battery again (targeted tests, analyze, format on the PR's touched files, and my old repros still pass).
- CRAP: new functions — keySlotCandidates (trivial), migrateLegacyKeySlots (loops/branches — count CC: for + if + for + if + if + ternary ≈ 7 — fine), roleKeyNames (extended — watch CRAP! it's a collection literal with spread-ifs; CC could rise. CI will tell.)

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.

   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).

  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.

host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical

blocks.text:
The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

Now the second fix — the missing-key degrade:
- `chainFor` throws `UnusableRoleChainException` (or `UnknownProviderRoleException`) when no usable entry — NEVER plain ConfigException for the no-usable-entry shape.
- Boot catches `UnusableRoleChainException` → stderr warn → legacy single-model path. Plain `ConfigException` still fails loud.
- Are there OTHER catch sites of `UnknownProviderRoleException` that now miss the new base type? Let me grep for catch sites of both exception types across the repo (including the app host / agent wiring / headless paths). If some caller catches ONLY `UnknownProviderRoleException` (the narrower type), a missing-key chain would now crash THAT caller with the un-caught `UnusableRoleChainException` — a real regression risk. Let me grep.

blocks.text:
The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. # gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry `baseUrl` (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.

The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

messages.preview: Migration machinery checks out (write-through with sanitized diagnostics, non-destructive, never leaks the secret). Now the critical impact check — every catch site of the exception hierarchy, since t…

blocks.text:
The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

Now the second fix — the missing-key degrade:
- `chainFor` throws `UnusableRoleChainException` (or `UnknownProviderRoleException`) when no usable entry — NEVER plain ConfigException for the no-usable-entry shape.
- Boot catches `UnusableRoleChainException` → stderr warn → legacy single-model path. Plain `ConfigException` still fails loud.
- Are there OTHER catch sites of `UnknownProviderRoleException` that now miss the new base type? Let me grep for catch sites of both exception types across the repo (including the app host / agent wiring / headless paths). If some caller catches ONLY `UnknownProviderRoleException` (the narrower type), a missing-key chain would now crash THAT caller with the un-caught `UnusableRoleChainException` — a real regression risk. Let me grep.

The mid-session call sites: `resolveRole` is called per-turn in compaction paths (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:36`, `task_executor.dart:547`, `host_wiring.dart:178`), guarded with `?.` and null-fallbacks — but `resolveRole` itself calls `chainFor` which can now throw `UnusableRoleChainException` (uncaught at those sites in either version — previously ConfigException, now UnusableRoleChainException, but UnusableRoleChainException IS-A ConfigException, so any `on ConfigException` catch keeps catching it).

Key insight: `UnusableRoleChainException extends ConfigException` — so EVERY existing `on ConfigException` handler in the codebase still catches both. The only behavior change is where code distinguished the two (only the boot). That's a clean, backward-compatible design. The boot boundary changed from `on UnknownProviderRoleException` to `on UnusableRoleChainException` — widening exactly as intended.

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }

blocks.text:
The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

Now the second fix — the missing-key degrade:
- `chainFor` throws `UnusableRoleChainException` (or `UnknownProviderRoleException`) when no usable entry — NEVER plain ConfigException for the no-usable-entry shape.
- Boot catches `UnusableRoleChainException` → stderr warn → legacy single-model path. Plain `ConfigException` still fails loud.
- Are there OTHER catch sites of `UnknownProviderRoleException` that now miss the new base type? Let me grep for catch sites of both exception types across the repo (including the app host / agent wiring / headless paths). If some caller catches ONLY `UnknownProviderRoleException` (the narrower type), a missing-key chain would now crash THAT caller with the un-caught `UnusableRoleChainException` — a real regression risk. Let me grep.

The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }
  }
  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that
  genuinely cannot bind (`claude-sonnet-4-5` over the openai canonical
  endpoint) instead of the stale-gateway fixture (which binds fine under
  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries
  (seed config, the issue #675 ambient-env JSON, the hub-row entries). No
  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.

The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

- `chainFor` throws `UnusableRoleChainException` (or `UnknownProviderRoleException`) when no usable entry — NEVER plain ConfigException for the no-usable-entry shape.

   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any

   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry

(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are

(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.

blocks.text:
The migration machinery is sound:
- `keys.save` writes through to the OS store, returns false on failure, and `lastSaveError` carries a `secureKeyDiagnosticLine`-sanitized diagnostic (never the secret — that's the established sanitizer for gh-1059).
- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

Now the second fix — the missing-key degrade:
- `chainFor` throws `UnusableRoleChainException` (or `UnknownProviderRoleException`) when no usable entry — NEVER plain ConfigException for the no-usable-entry shape.
- Boot catches `UnusableRoleChainException` → stderr warn → legacy single-model path. Plain `ConfigException` still fails loud.
- Are there OTHER catch sites of `UnknownProviderRoleException` that now miss the new base type? Let me grep for catch sites of both exception types across the repo (including the app host / agent wiring / headless paths). If some caller catches ONLY `UnknownProviderRoleException` (the narrower type), a missing-key chain would now crash THAT caller with the un-caught `UnusableRoleChainException` — a real regression risk. Let me grep.

The migration machinery is sound:

- `migrateLegacyKeySlots` guards: skip when store unavailable; skip when canonical already populated; copy from legacy only; non-destructive (legacy kept); `break` after one source (one stranded source per canonical slot); notice names slots/endpoint, never the value.

One consideration: the migration runs BEFORE `roleKeyNames` snapshot preload? Order in fah_runapp: the migration loop is placed right after some stderr writer, before resolution. But the snapshot: `SecureKeyCache.read` reads `_snapshot` — for the migration to SEE the legacy slot's value, the legacy slot must be in the snapshot (preload) — or does `read` hit the store? `read` is snapshot-only (line: "Synchronous read from the snapshot (null when absent)"). So migration only works if the legacy slot names are in the preload set. What names does the boot preload? `roleKeyNames` (startup.dart) — which was EXTENDED to include the whole slot family for both the unpinned and pinned ref legs. So the preload set covers the family. But there's a subtle ordering issue: `roleKeyNames` must be computed and preloaded BEFORE `migrateLegacyKeySlots` runs. Let me verify the boot order: preload(roleKeyNames(...)) → migrate → resolve. Also: if the canonical slot is NOT in the preload set, `keys.save` writes through to the store AND updates the snapshot — fine.

Conversely: what if a legacy slot holds the value but is NOT in the preload set? Then `keys.read(legacy)` = null → no migration → resolution fallback ALSO reads the snapshot → null → key-missing. The extended `roleKeyNames` covers exactly the family shapes, so both legs preload the family. The pinned-leg addition: `if (ref.apiKeyName != null && ref.baseUrl != null) ...keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl!)` — hmm, wait: for a PINNED ref whose endpoint is the catalog DEFAULT, `_endpointScopedKeyNames` returns [] (sameEndpoint → no scoped slot)... but the old `roleKeyNames` had `if (_refNeedsEndpointSlot(ref)) keyNameFor(baseUrl)` — only when NOT default. The new pinned leg adds `keySlotCandidates(baseUrl)` for every pinned ref with a baseUrl — including default-endpoint pinned refs (the incident shape: "the incident pin sat on kimi's default URL"). That's the deliberate widening. But it also means for a pinned ref on a default endpoint, the snapshot now carries `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM` — a slot it didn't carry before. That's the fix (the incident: pin on default URL, key on host-scoped slot of the default URL... wait, `_missingPinFallback` probes `keySlotCandidates(ref.baseUrl)` = [record-scoped?, host-scoped] — for the incident: `keyNameFor(url, providerName: 'kimi-ira')` (record) and `keyNameFor(url)` (host). The key sat on the host-scoped slot. Preload must carry both → the new pinned leg does exactly that.

There's a potential preload-overhead concern (2 more keychain reads per pinned ref — bounded, fine).

# gh-1570 rework — CI red head `ba5c00d3` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Five CI legs were red on the PR head (`Quality gate` is the aggregate; the real
failures were `PTY/CLI integration (shard 0/3)`, `Core tests (shard 1/4)`,
`Core tests (shard 3/4)` and `Hostile ambient env`). Two root causes — both
leg-1 regressions against existing blocking contracts:

1. **L9 degrade dropped *servable* saved pairs and bricked the boot**
   (`PTY/CLI integration shard 0` — 2 failures in
   `test/integration/poisoned_provider_boot_test.dart`).
   The first implementation kept the saved `model`+`baseUrl` pair on an
   endpoint-conflict degrade only when the pair spelled the *degraded kind's
   own default endpoint*. A persisted `chatgpt-codex` config pointed at any
   other endpoint (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write, a LAN gateway, a
   local server) had its pair dropped wholesale — the boot then died with
   `ConfigException: provider "openai-completions" requires --model <id>`
   (+ `crash.log`), breaking gh-760's blocking invariant *a persisted
   provider can never brick the CLI* and its pinned pair-guard test
   (`exit 0`, turn completes on the saved endpoint, no `crash.log`).
   The degrade warning also started printing `the saved baseUrl "null"`.
   The ticket's own E2 wording is the correct arbiter: *"restore either
   rebuilds a valid binding or refuses cleanly"* — the degrade refuses the
   saved KIND, not every endpoint it was pointed at.

2. **Queue-editor fixtures still encoded the legacy kind-only entry**
   (`Core tests shard 1/4` — 12 failures in
   `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`; `Core tests shard 3/4` +
   `Hostile ambient env` — 1 failure in
   `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`).
   gh-1570 (AC6/M5) rightly rejects an identity-less `openai-completions`
   queue entry (no record name, no `baseUrl`) instead of silently riding
   openrouter.ai — but these two pre-existing suites build their runtime
   from kind-only fixtures, so every editor branch under test crashed with
   the new `ConfigException` before reaching its assertions. The
   production semantics are correct and kept (the PR's own
   `providers_queue_test.dart` pins the rejection); the fixtures now carry
   a real `baseUrl`, preserving each test's intent (editor branch
   coverage, hub-row rendering).

The perf-budget failures seen in one local concurrent rerun
(`redact/perf`, `structured_ledger_perf`, `wrap_ansi_line_perf`) are
CPU-contention artifacts — none touches provider code; all 16 pass solo.
The two PTY timing failures in the local shard run are the known
host-load flake family: `header_badge_pty_test.dart` is flake-quarantined
(`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, issue #1469 — CI never runs it) and
`composer_tui_grid_pty_test.dart` passes 6/6 solo.

## Approach

- **`lib/src/cli/startup.dart`** — the degrade keep/drop decision is now the
  binding's verdict, the same single validating constructor every other
  entry point answers to: new `_degradedPairResolves()` resolves the saved
  `modelId`+`baseUrl` under the degraded kind via
  `ProviderModelBinding.resolve(provenance: restore)`; the pair rides the
  degraded boot when it validates (gh-760's mock-endpoint partial write,
  the codex-over-openrouter default spelling) and is dropped only when the
  constructor rejects it (e.g. a claude-family id pinned over
  `api.openai.com`) or a half is blank:
  `keepSavedPair = !degraded || _degradedPairResolves(provider, saved)`.
  The AC3/H2 partial-override check below it is unchanged.

  ```dart
  bool _degradedPairResolves(String degradedKind, CliConfig saved) {
    if (saved.modelId.trim().isEmpty || saved.baseUrl.trim().isEmpty) {
      return false;
    }
    try {
      ProviderModelBinding.resolve(
        providerKind: degradedKind,
        modelId: saved.modelId,
        baseUrl: saved.baseUrl,
        provenance: BindingProvenance.restore,
      );
      return true;
    } on ConfigException {
      return false;
    }

  ```

- **`test/cli/startup_test.dart`** — the L9 drop test now pins a pair that

  `openai-completions` and must be kept per gh-760); added the gh-760 AC1
  keep test (foreign mock endpoint, turn-completing pair never bricks).
- **`test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart`** — fixtures carry
  `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:1/v1` on their `openai-completions` entries

  production code changed for this class — the runtime rejection is the
  AC6/M5 fix working as designed.

- `lib/src/cli/startup.dart` — binding-arbiter degrade (L9/E2 reconciled with gh-760).
- `test/cli/startup_test.dart` — L9 drop fixture corrected to an unbindable pair; gh-760 AC1 keep test added.
- `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` — queue fixtures carry `baseUrl` (AC6).
- `test/cli/settings_flow_providers_queue_test.dart` — same fixture fix.
